Laezel meets Vlaaktih as a hologram. Avatar can decide if she accepts her orders to kill the prisoner or refuse. In both cases, the planecaster is activated.If you refuse, Vlaakith orders the inquisitor if alive to kill you if you try to exit the room or theatens to hunt you down if he's already dead. Orphan Laezel automatically accepts Vlaakith's orders.

Vlaaktih appears as a hologram and Laezel meets her for the first time. Avatar can decide if she accepts her orders to kill the prisoner or refuse. In both cases, the planecaster is activated.If you refuse, Vlaakith orders the inquisitor if alive to kill you if you try to exit the room or theatens to hunt you down if he's already dead. If Laezel is not yet convinced to side with the player, they have a chance to do it here if they refuse.

The player attempts to remove their tadpole with the device, not realising that it will kill them as it does so. The player has opportunity to save themselves from the machine. If they fail or refuse those opportunities, Daisy will intervene. Variations based on whether the doctor and Lae'zel are present or not.

Laezel reacts on the Zaithisk being a lie. Should point to the Inqusitor if the conflict with him hasn't started, or at the inquisitor's office if it has. If Vlaakith betrayal has already happened, should point that she needs time to reflect on this.
context: Lae'zel is convinced the zaith'isk (a strange device of taut flesh and pockmarked metal) is Vlaakith's cure and a sacred duty, and she refuses to accept that it is killing those who use it. The player arrives and attempts to force her aside and either take control of the device or stop it from harming anyone. A doctor and infirmary staff are present, and the surrounding dialogue reflects Lae'zel’s loyalty to Vlaakith and her belief she has already entrusted the player with her "might." If the scene proceeds, the machine can fatally harm its user, eventually explodes, and the doctor will call the guards; choices and prior events (including Vlaakith’s orders elsewhere) influence whether Lae'zel resists or can be persuaded.
